subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration feasibility & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Walker <sam.walker@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration feasibility & next steps

Hi Sam — thanks again for taking time to chat today. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps. Please tell me if I missed anything.

Key pain points you called out:
- Peak latency during holiday spikes (search + personalization flows) is causing slow page loads and cart abandonment.
- Current embeddings pipeline is expensive and re-runs frequently; team wants cheaper, incremental updates and faster reranking.
- Need structured outputs for downstream fulfillment systems (order extraction) and safe function calls for price lookups.

What we discussed as fit for Redwood:
- Hosting a ranking+generation hybrid: embeddings for first-pass candidate retrieval, then lightweight reranker using Redwood embeddings/reranking to reduce calls to your heavier model.
- Function calling for price lookups / inventory checks; streaming responses for UX-sensitive flows to show partial results while we finalize the backend call.
- SDK: we can provide a small changeset to your backend to support function-calling signatures and streaming client; no model retraining required.

Action items / next steps:
1) Redwood to share a 1-pager + SOC2 answers (attached).
2) Acme to confirm a PO C scope (1–2 endpoints: product search rerank + order extraction).
3) Internal technical kickoff with your infra team + our engineer (Dylan) next week; propose Thu 3/18 10am PT.
4) Draft estimate / POC timeline (2–3 weeks) and success criteria (latency 50% drop at p95 for rerank path; 30% cost reduction on embeddings pipeline).

Attachments: redwood-runtime-onepager.pdf, acme-soc2-answers.xlsx, poc-scope.docx

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa — this is great, thanks for the clear notes. A couple quick clarifications: 
- For reranking, we'd likely want a deterministic fallback to our existing ranker if the Redwood latency spikes, is that supported by routing policies?
- For the order extraction piece, we need structured JSON output with confidence scores for each field (order_id, sku, qty).

We can confirm PO C scope on our side; I'll loop in product ops to agree the success criteria. Thu 3/18 10am PT works for the technical call for us.

I'll upload a short dataset sample (sanitized) for Dylan to review before the call.

— Sam
Sam Walker

sam.walker@acmeretail.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration feasibility & next steps

Hi Sam — appreciate the sample offer. A few technical notes ahead of Thu's call so we can make the most of the kickoff: 

1) Routing & fallbacks: yes, Redwood supports policy-based routing. We can configure a latency-first route with an automatic fallback to your deterministic model variant when p95 exceeds your threshold. We'll bring the console demo to show how that looks in practice.

2) Structured outputs & confidences: Redwood's function-calling + structured output modes can emit JSON following a user-provided schema and return per-field confidences. We typically implement a wrapper schema and a lightweight verifier to enforce types and confidence thresholds.

3) SDK changes: minimal — our SDK will need to be called with a new options object for function signatures and streaming handlers. Example changes:
- add .onStream(tokenHandler) callback for progressive UI updates
- pass functions: [{name:\"price_lookup\", params_schema: {...}}] in the request payload

4) Embeddings/reranking: For cost efficiency we recommend a two-stage approach: cached dense embeddings with incremental updates + a shallow reranker on a quantized candidate set. That should cut embedding QPS by ~40–60% for typical traffic patterns.

I'll attach a short POC checklist and a minimal server side SDK patch you can drop into a staging service (see attachment: poc-scope.docx). Please confirm the dataset upload link and I'll pre-check formatting.

Thanks — Dylan
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference
